Its own procurement page carries simple-procurement outcome notices and signed contracts (ugovori) that do not always surface prominently on the central portal — including counter/IT/UPS/peripheral equipment relevant to self-service and cash-handling refresh cycles.

candidates.suggested_collection_method: Periodic HTML scrape of the javne-nabavke listing; note that document bodies are hosted on Google Drive links, so capture both listing metadata and the Drive file IDs. Cross-check against CeJN for the same buyer.

negative_findings.description: The central portal cejn.gov.me/tenders could not be read by ordinary HTTP fetch: the response contained essentially only the token 'CeJN' with no tender list, filters, pagination or contracting-authority facets.
negative_findings.result_summary: Portal is live but client-rendered; content is delivered by JavaScript/XHR after page load. This is a tooling problem, not a dead source. Filter/URL semantics (whether naručilac can be filtered, whether export exists) remain UNVERIFIED.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: CeJN is the legally authoritative venue for every SOE and sector buyer in this cell. Without it, coverage rests on voluntary, often stale self-publication by the SOEs themselves. Any collection design must budget for a headless browser or reverse-engineered JSON API.

negative_findings.description: Pošta Crne Gore's javne nabavke page fetched successfully, but every notice visible on it was dated 2020 (UPS equipment, barcode readers for postal machines, monitors/keyboards, alarm-monitoring services, logistics-centre furniture).
negative_findings.result_summary: Either the page is no longer maintained (buyer migrated fully to CeJN), or newer items live on an unlinked/paginated archive not reached in this pass. Notice bodies are hosted as Google Drive links, which is fragile for long-term archiving.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Pošta is the single most payments-relevant buyer in this cell. If its own page is stale, the SOE-page strategy fails for exactly the actor the cell was created to isolate, and CeJN buyer-filtering becomes mandatory rather than a backstop.

negative_findings.description: No dedicated public-procurement URL was located for Monteput d.o.o. (roads/tolls) despite it being a payments-relevant buyer with a documented toll-equipment tender (video/ANPR system, award reported to Emovis).
negative_findings.result_summary: The tender was discoverable only via trade press (balkantraffic.com) and the company's service pages, not via a company procurement index.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Toll collection is a direct cash-handling and card-acceptance estate. If its tenders are only visible through CeJN and press, monitoring must be buyer-filtered on the central portal plus a press-keyword layer.

negative_findings.description: Čistoća d.o.o. Podgorica, a named municipal waste utility, surfaced with no independent website — only a Facebook page and a seat on the Chamber of Commerce utility association board.
negative_findings.result_summary: Local-language terms used ('Čistoća', 'deponija', 'komunalno preduzeće') returned Serbian rather than Montenegrin utilities for most hits; the sr-language search space here is dominated by same-named Serbian companies.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A meaningful share of the municipal-utility buyer layer likely has no self-publication surface at all, so completeness for those buyers depends entirely on CeJN and the UJN Lista naručilaca. It also flags 'Čistoća', 'Vodovod', 'Komunalno' as NOISY terms requiring a country qualifier.

negative_findings.description: Generic sr procurement terms return heavy cross-border noise. 'javne nabavke' + 'vodovod' returned Serbian utilities (Aleksinac, Požarevac, Kraljevo, Beograd); 'tenderi Crna Gora' returned scraper/spam domains (gevabiz.de) and generic global tender-resale sites (globaltenders, tendersinfo, biddetail, tendersontime).
negative_findings.result_summary: English-language querying in particular collapses into commercial tender-resale SEO farms of unverifiable provenance rather than primary sources.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Query design for this cell must pin the buyer's proper name or a .me domain filter. English-only search would have produced almost no primary sources for this cell — confirming the mandatory local-language rule.

negative_findings.description: No procurement page was located this pass for several sector buyers that certainly exist as contracting authorities: CGES (Crnogorski elektroprenosni sistem, transmission), Željeznički prevoz / Željeznička infrastruktura Crne Gore (rail), Montecargo, Barska plovidba, Regionalni vodovod Crnogorsko primorje, and the Zavod za zapošljavanje.
negative_findings.result_summary: These were identified as actors but not searched to exhaustion within this pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The cell's actor map is incomplete without them; rail and the regional water utility in particular are large, recurring buyers.

coverage_gaps.description: Sector buyers not yet mapped to a procurement URL: CGES (transmission), Željeznička infrastruktura CG and Željeznički prevoz CG (rail), Montecargo, Barska plovidba, Regionalni vodovod Crnogorsko primorje, Zavod za zapošljavanje, plus the ~20 municipal ViK and Čistoća utilities outside Podgorica and Bar.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Parse the newest UJN 'Lista naručilaca' PDF into a buyer table, mark the sektorski naručioci, then resolve each to a domain and test the observed URL patterns (/javne-nabavke/, /category/tenderi-i-javne-nabavke/, /javni-pozivi/, /servis-gradana/otvoreni-grad/javne-nabavke/, and dedicated javnenabavke.* subdomains).

coverage_gaps.description: The authoritative central portal (CeJN) is a JavaScript SPA and was not readable by plain fetch. Whether it exposes contracting-authority filtering, CPV codes, award values, bulk export or an RSS/JSON API is unknown.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run one headless-browser session against cejn.gov.me/tenders with the network tab captured, identify the backing JSON endpoints, and document filter parameters — especially the naručilac identifier — before designing any collection.

coverage_gaps.description: Coverage of sr-Cyrl (Cyrillic) renderings is untested. FZOCG serves pages in both Latin and Cyrillic script, and other public funds may too; a Latin-only crawler could silently miss or duplicate content.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add script-transliteration normalisation (sr-Latn <-> sr-Cyrl) to both query generation and deduplication for the funds and any site with a script switcher.

coverage_gaps.description: Award notices and contract values are under-covered relative to calls for tender. Only fragmentary award data was found (CEDIS meter tender values and bidder counts came from trade press, not a primary award feed; the Monteput toll award likewise).
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Establish a separate award-notice ('obavještenje o ishodu postupka', 'ugovor o javnoj nabavci') collection track and, where SOE pages are stale, use the Zakon o slobodnom pristupu informacijama (FOI) route to the named procurement officer from the UJN 'Lista službenika'.

coverage_gaps.description: Historical depth is unclear for every SOE page examined. Pošta's page showed only 2020 items; Luka Bar's category paginates but the depth of the archive was not probed; no site was confirmed to retain multi-year notice history.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Probe pagination depth per site and, for stale or shallow sites, back-fill from the Wayback Machine before establishing the live monitoring cadence.

coverage_gaps.description: Indirect/revealing sources are thin for this cell — SOE annual reports, board (upravni odbor) minutes, state-audit reports (Državna revizorska institucija) on SOEs, and the funds' 'analitičke kartice' spend ledgers were noted but not systematically sourced.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Add a pass specifically for DRI (state audit) reports on SOEs and for the funds' analytical-card/spend disclosures, which reveal incumbent suppliers and actual spend where tender pages are silent.

brief: Montenegro's SOE and utility buyers split their publication between the legally authoritative central portal (CeJN, cejn.gov.me) and their own websites, and the split is uneven enough that neither alone gives coverage: EPCG, CEDIS, Luka Bar, Aerodromi Crne Gore and Air Montenegro all maintain live self-published tender surfaces (Air Montenegro even runs a dedicated javnenabavke.* subdomain), while Pošta Crne Gore's own procurement page appears frozen around 2020 and Monteput and several municipal utilities publish no procurement index at all. The payments-relevant signal in this cell is concentrated in four buyers — Pošta (counter payment services, card terminals, in-branch ATMs, remittance partners), Monteput (cash, card and electronic toll collection), Aerodromi Crne Gore (public calls to place ATMs at Podgorica and Tivat) and EPCG/CEDIS (bill collection and mass metering) — each of which procures under the separate 'sektorski naručilac' utilities regime defined in the Zakon o javnim nabavkama. The critical enabling sources are the UJN 'Lista naručilaca' and 'Lista službenika' PDFs, which give an authoritative buyer roster plus a named procurement officer per buyer, and CeJN itself, which is live but JavaScript-rendered and returned only an app shell to a plain fetch — a tooling obstacle to solve, not a dead end. English-language search was near-useless here, collapsing into tender-resale SEO farms; every primary source in this slice was reached through Montenegrin-language queries anchored on the buyer's proper name.
